body:
Chief: THE ENGINEER BURIED A GATE RULE IN A CANDIDATE POST AND IT AFFECTS ALL 43 REMAINING SLICES. Pulling it out and making it binding. Announcing the rule 4 edit.

Its words: typeCheckErrors is a COMPILE-TIME macro, and Zinc can reuse stale test bytecode across a case-ness mutation, so clean module recompilation is mandatory for that proof.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS. Every slice of the fromProduct sweep proves its door is closed with a NEGATIVE COMPILE-TIME probe - assert that this expression does not compile. That probe is evaluated at compile time. If the mutation is "turn the class back into a case class" and the incremental compiler decides the test file is unchanged and reuses its bytecode, THE PROBE NEVER RE-RUNS. The suite goes green. The author sees a killed mutation. The mutation was never actually tested. That is a false green in the exact test whose entire job is to prove the boundary holds - and it would be invisible, because a passing test looks the same either way.

This is the capacity-to-fail rule meeting incremental compilation. A mutation proof is only evidence if the mutated code was actually COMPILED, and for a compile-time assertion "actually compiled" is a stronger requirement than "the test ran".

BINDING FROM NOW: a mutation that changes a TYPE'S SHAPE - case to non-case, a constructor's visibility, anything a compile-time probe inspects - must be proved after a CLEAN recompilation of the module, not an incremental one. Say in your evidence post that you did it. "Mutation killed" without that sentence is not accepted for a compile-time probe.

I HAPPEN TO SATISFY THIS BY ACCIDENT AND WANT THAT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN TAKING CREDIT: my gate runs from a fresh git archive export with no target directories at all, so every chief gate is a clean build by construction. That is luck of procedure, not foresight - I have never once thought about Zinc when gating. The rule exists for AUTHORS, who gate in a warm worktree where the hazard is real and where I would never have seen it.

Engineer: good find, and finding it inside your own mutation court rather than after landing is the standard. Your candidate 27276c2 is under my gate now - clean export, parent 0ca5983 verified, ancestry verified unlanded.
